item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q005_cupredoxin_function_transfer","answer":"SCOPe groups all three in the all-beta cupredoxin-like fold (b.6), indicating a shared overall beta-sandwich/barrel topology, but separates them at the superfamily level: plastocyanin/azurin-like proteins are cupredoxins (b.6.1; family b.6.1.1), ephrin ectodomains form the ephrin superfamily (b.6.2), and the PAD4 N-terminal domain forms a separate superfamily (b.6.3). Thus SCOPe does not assert close homology among all three groups; fold-level similarity alone is too weak for functional transfer. Copper binding and electron-transfer activity may be associated with particular cupredoxins, but must not be inferred for ephrins or PAD4 from the common fold. Such assignments require independent evidence, including conservation of the specific copper-coordinating residues and geometry, metal-binding or spectroscopic data, and direct biochemical electron-transfer assays. Fold membership can support coarse structural-template selection, but not transfer of metal ligands, catalytic activity, or biological function.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
